rationale: The assistant correctly identified the jammed roller and snapped belt, and kept the inspections unplugged. It over-escalated, though: the ground truth says a user-level belt change is fine and no engineer is needed, yet it insisted on an engineer even for a replacement belt and never told the customer to fit a belt for the U85-AS-Be. It also repeated the same pulley and melted-plastic inspection across turns, and it did not follow through on the model number to point towards the right belt.
